messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
The first half of the edits should have reached you just now. Thank you very much for giving me the opportunity to work on your novel. It is an ambitious book and highly relevant. In the second portion of my edits, I’ll discuss the novel and my overall assessment in greater depth. That part will include a 15-20 page editorial letter, followed by a video chat that we’ll schedule after you receive the letter.

I recommend first going through the manuscript and all of the comments without revising or changing anything, simply absorbing the notes. Afterward, give yourself some time to consider how you may want to approach the edits. Every comment comes from the perspective of helping the novel achieve your intended purpose and enabling readers to connect with both the story and its themes. I also recommend holding off on any major changes until you receive the editorial letter. It will address more specific points, offer a detailed overview of the novel’s elements, break down how the piece moves, and supply additional examples and resources to support you during revision.

I also like to remind authors, as they begin reading comments throughout a draft, that I will ask many questions about particular sections or moments. Those questions are not requests for answers to me; instead, they indicate matters that should be made clearer on the page so readers are less confused and the prose and story continue to flow. Each comment is intended to show where the story creates confusion or requires more work. With all of that said, you are free to proceed however you prefer and begin editing today! I understand that impulse. Ultimately, it is your novel, and my role is to support you.

I also want to be clear that my comments must not be used to train AI or entered into an LLM or AI writer for assistance with revising stories or generating new ones.

Please tell me if there is anything specific you would like me to explain further or offer more insight about in the editorial letter. I’ll make sure it is included. The letter will also address more of your questions and identify additional things to watch for.

Thank you! We’ll talk soon.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I’m only now seeing this.
I’m on vacation, so I’ll go through the comments and then give myself time to sit with them. In any case, I’ll be able to focus better once I’m home.

I’ve just read the opening pages and their comments. I understand your points and am looking forward to talking about some of them more thoroughly. Certain choices I made were deliberate, but they clearly weren’t effective. I can explain them when we meet, once I’ve seen your complete notes/letter. This is extremely useful because I think I need to discover different ways of building a feeling of mystery and the unknown.

We can discuss more later, but I already know this will help a great deal. There’s a lot of work ahead...and plenty of questions to ask. :)

Bela

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Am I understanding correctly that I should review everything first, and then approve the work and pay you? I don’t want to hold you up, but I also want to follow the proper process. Please let me know. I can move through the comments quickly and ask you any questions that come up.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The choice is yours! You may review every comment before approving the work, or you can approve it now. In either case, you can still ask questions, request that I elaborate on something, or have me expand on it in the letter. Approving the work now won't end either the contract or our communication. Upwork will also approve things automatically after a week or 2, regardless of whether you approve them yourself.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Good morning from here on the East Coast,

As I mentioned earlier, many of the points you’ve raised so far make complete sense. I could tell that things felt wrong, but I couldn’t identify why. The major challenge now is HOW to correct them. I’ve quickly gone through roughly half of your comments, and while reading them I start wondering, WTF did I write?? I know those reactions are normal. You begin questioning whether the whole thing is complete crap, and so on. BUT this is a positive development. I’ve never received comments and suggestions this comprehensive, and I can see the problems now: places where I rush, areas without enough detail...

The difficult work starts now, and I’m overwhelmed, which I know is normal. One side of me feels that I NEED to release this book ASAP because it matters so much. At the same time, I worry that I may never be able to repair some of the chaos. Thinking about the TIME involved makes me panic. That’s simply my impatience showing.

In any event, this is incredible. Your work is precisely what I needed and had been seeking. Everything makes sense so far.

I’ll continue reading and take notes in a separate document rather than making significant changes. I’m excited and hope I can manage this. LOL.

I’m releasing the payment, and I’ll keep reviewing everything while waiting for your letter.

We’ll talk soon,

Bela

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I want to reassure you that your novel is absolutely not complete crap! All of the necessary pieces are present: the characters, the world, the story, and the emotions. As you said, the next step is to sharpen those pieces so the novel creates the impact you intend.

What you’re feeling is both normal and valid. Producing strong literary work requires time. If urgency or timing is a concern, I can add publishing guidance to my letter to help you decide which publication path best suits your novel and your intention. Would you find that useful?

I’ll complete the letter and return it to you by or before 7/20.

I’m confident that you can do this!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you for the note! I understand those periods of fear and the desire for validation. Most of the time, though, I tell myself I don’t care what anyone thinks about my writing because, in many respects, I write for myself. As writers, we’re subjective and can fall in love with what we create, but are we ever truly capable of objectivity? Philosophy for 4th.

I still don’t know whether I’ll self publish. Every book I’ve released has been self published through my own imprint, and I’ve handled both the covers and interior formatting myself. The results aren’t perfect...but I understand how difficult finding an agent can be because I’ve tried before. AND, I may prefer to retain greater control over my work. I’m also aware of how challenging marketing is, so I remain uncertain. Money isn’t why I’m doing this, although I would love to earn a living from writing one day. I’m realistic about it...I have a day job. I also have a short list of small indie presses that I might approach after the manuscript is ready. If I choose to self publish, I’ll hire both a cover designer and an interior formatter. Atticus, if you know it, has limitations and isn’t the best option.

I’ve finished reading through the manuscript and am still processing everything. I’ve decided to begin examining your comments more closely on Monday, after I return home. It’s too difficult to concentrate amid the crazy but enjoyable family chaos.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you again, and I hope you enjoy what remains of your weekend!
I have an incredible number of typos, ha ha.
Apparently, typing without my glasses isn’t a very good plan. :)

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Good morning from the East Coast,

I did a quick read of your letter last night, and today I’m going to slow down and work through everything carefully.

It’s extraordinarily helpful. Even during that fast initial read, I understood much of what you were explaining.

I’m available most afternoons, although certain mornings are more crowded for me. If possible, I’d prefer for us to meet sooner rather than later. Most of my questions concern the structure, particularly at the beginning, and I’d also appreciate clarification about some of your other points.

I believe I’ve decided to self-publish. Securing an agent is extremely difficult, though I do have a couple of indie presses on my list. Before the manuscript was edited, I sent a few feelers to agents just for fun. So far there has been nothing beyond a few nos, although at least those rejections took some time. Traditional publishing would also take forever, leave me with less control over my work, and still require me to handle my own marketing... I’d really value your perspective on this. I know how challenging traditional publication is, and I don’t want to spend time needlessly. This book is about my message and my words. Naturally, making money from it would be wonderful, but that isn’t my main objective. Publishing without an agent could be an option...but only with the right place.

Social media is full of discussion and protests involving data centers (and AI). I have a strong feeling in my gut but can’t tell whether it’s excitement or anxiety. I want to publish this as soon as possible because the timing feels so right. Of course, I also want the book to be as perfect as possible.

After our work is complete and I’ve made all my revisions, what should my next step be? Would a copyedit alone be sufficient after this? My budget is somewhat tight, but I’ll find a way. I simply need to plan financially for the copyedit, cover, and interior format.

Can you recommend anyone, especially a cover designer? Perhaps that person also provides interior formatting. Copyediting will be crucial because I’ve inserted many new scenes in response to your earlier comments.

I realize I’m thinking too far ahead. I just feel pulled toward this.

For scheduling, I’m free tomorrow afternoon or in the early evening after 1pm EST but before 8 pm EST. On Thursday and Friday, I can meet any time before 4pm EST, and on Saturday I’m available any time after 12pm EST. My schedule is tighter the following week: Monday works between 1pm and 4pm EST, while Tuesday is open anytime.

FYI, I’ve added about 15k words. Most of that consists of new scenes, additional information about Matt, greater detail about the world, and more character development, esp. for everyone (the men, Sophie). I’ll also be deleting material. That is another reason I need to determine what the next editing stages should be!

You’re amazing! I simply wanted you to know that.

Bela

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hello! I’m happy that you’d prefer to meet sooner rather than later. Would Thursday from 1:30 PM to 3 PM EDT/EST work for you? I can address the questions in your message during our meeting, unless you would rather have me write the responses in a document and send them to you.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I’m responding by email because I’m away from my computer, but Thursday at 1:30 my time works perfectly.

I can send you a couple of broader questions about ideas I’m considering, and we can likely cover the remaining questions during the call.

I’ve spent a great deal of time thinking about the book’s beginning, especially those opening chapters. I have several ideas that I’d like to discuss with you.

Later, I’ll send a short summary of what I’m considering so you have time to think it over before our meeting.

Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Great! We can hold the meeting here through Upwork’s video meeting feature. I’ll watch for your summary and questions. I’m looking forward to our conversation!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I’ve been working through the possibilities for the beginning, specifically the first 3 chapters. I like using Envoy as the opening, but you’re correct that his role in this book isn’t that of the rogue AI. I wanted him introduced in this book, yet the opening currently doesn’t connect fully with the rest.

One possibility:
I could retain the chapter but relocate it to the end as a kind of epilogue. I’d revise a few details so it appears that Sage never actually shut him down. Instead, he was only pretending, then reboots at the end, with the final words being I am God...
What do you think? I’m conflicted about it. Would he remain an unresolved thread, even in an epilogue? I also like the book’s present ending and think it works effectively, though editing is needed. Because of that, I’m uncertain whether this idea would succeed. I’d love to keep the chapter, but if it doesn’t go at the end, I don’t know where else to use it.

For chapter 2 (Beginnings):
A) I would remove a substantial portion and convert what remains to 3rd person, making it sound as though someone is narrating a story. I’d then transition somehow into Chapter 3 Mortal Life so it’s evident that the narrative has moved into Sage’s perspective. I’m unsure of the most effective way to accomplish that, or whether the idea even makes sense. I would also remove the first two paragraphs from Mortal LIfe.

B) I could eliminate Beginnings completely.

Chapter 3 (Mortal Life)
Another option is to turn the first 2 paragraphs into a prologue—I know opinions about prologues are divided—and then begin the chapter as described above.

Hopefully this isn’t overly confusing. I can see multiple possibilities, and I definitely want to preserve Mortal Life, except for the first 2 paragraphs. I could delete all or most of Beginnings and perhaps shift it to 3rd person, while moving Envoy to the ending or sacrificing him. :)

I’ve also been considering the voice used for Sage during childhood. I agree that it can sound almost like a YA novel. I’m drawn to the idea that her voice reflects who she is in that particular moment, allowing us to see the world through her eyes, but I need more direction on how to handle it. I understand the problems caused by moving between story mode with future Sage and present day Sage. I’ve revised much of the book to address that, apart from the earlier chapters discussed above.

I’ll be glad to hear your thoughts tomorrow!

There are several other topics we can discuss tomorrow as well.

Bela

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I have no idea how the sunglasses emoji appeared there. Strange! What it was meant to say is: B

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I just wanted to confirm that I received this and will be prepared to talk it through on our call. See you shortly!
